title: Buying and using the bat
target: How to get the baseball bat into a player's hands in Supermarket Simulator, and what the game says to use it on.
prerequisites: A shop that has been opened for the day

steps.do: Buy the bat from the market rather than waiting to find one.
steps.because: the game names a bat sale item and sets the player an objective to buy one from market (BatSaleItem, _buyBatObjective)

steps.do: Pick it out of the tool wheel once you own it.
steps.because: the game keeps a handler for the tool wheel's input hint, which is how it tells a player to hold a key and choose the bat (ToolWheelInputHintHandler, _openBatHint)

steps.do: Aim it at the shoplifter rather than at the stock.
steps.because: the game's own description says to hit the shoplifter and force them to drop the stolen items (_useBatDescription, _hitShoplifter)

steps.do: Swing and expect the goods to fall.
steps.because: the shoplifter's half of that exchange is kept in an interaction of its own (NetworkShoplifterInteraction)

steps.do: Watch the swing rather than guessing the reach.
steps.because: a swing and a bat swing are named beside an idle of its own (Swing_Bat, BaseballBatSwing, baseballidle)

steps.do: Keep the bat in the tool wheel rather than on a shelf.
steps.because: the bat has an icon of its own and a mesh with its own sheets (T_Icon_BaseballBat, SM_BaseballBat, M_BaseballBat)

commonMistakes: Looking for the bat in the shop's own stock list instead of the market.
Carrying the bat in a hand that was needed for the counter.
Swinging at the shelf the thief is standing next to rather than at the thief.
Assuming a hit ends the theft rather than making the thief drop what was taken.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
